feature: Add Mobile Navigation Menu to Landing Page
workflow_rationale: This is a simple, single-file UI enhancement that only adds a hamburger menu to the existing navigation component. No database changes, no API changes, just frontend state management and responsive UI.

phases.name: Add Mobile Hamburger Menu
phases.description: Convert Navigation component to client component and add hamburger menu with slide-in panel for mobile users

subtasks.description: Add mobile hamburger menu to Navigation component

changes: Add 'use client' directive to enable useState
Add useState for mobile menu open/close state
Replace mobile 'Başla' button with hamburger icon button
Add slide-in mobile menu panel with overlay
Include all navigation links (Özellikler, Fiyatlandırma, Giriş Yap) in mobile menu
Add Ücretsiz Dene CTA button in mobile menu
Add close button (X) in mobile menu header
Style with Tailwind animations and transitions

checks: On mobile viewport (<768px), hamburger icon is visible
Clicking hamburger opens slide-in menu from right
Mobile menu shows all navigation links
Clicking X button closes the menu
Clicking a nav link closes the menu and navigates

subtasks.notes: Created client component components/landing/navigation.tsx with mobile hamburger menu. Menu slides in from right with backdrop overlay, includes close button (X) and closes on link clicks. Desktop navigation remains unchanged with hidden md:flex pattern. Follows sidebar.tsx pattern for transitions and z-index layering.

acceptance_criteria: Mobile users can access all navigation links via hamburger menu
No layout shift or console errors

verification_steps.name: Mobile Viewport Test
verification_steps.command: Open browser DevTools, set viewport to 375px width
verification_steps.expected_outcome: Hamburger menu visible, desktop nav hidden

verification_steps.name: Desktop Viewport Test
verification_steps.command: Open browser DevTools, set viewport to 1024px width

verification_strategy.reasoning: Low risk UI-only change. Manual browser testing is sufficient since this is a visual/interactive feature. No business logic to unit test. TypeScript and linting ensure code quality.

unit_tests.reasoning: Simple UI component with no complex logic - manual testing is more appropriate
